## Natural history notes

A very large woodpecker characterized by its black body, bold white stripes on the face and neck, long chisel-like bill, and prominent red crest. In Florida, it is found in mature forests, pine flatwoods, cypress swamps, hammocks, wooded parks, and forested wetlands where large trees and dead wood are available. It feeds mainly on carpenter ants, beetle larvae, termites, and other insects, often excavating large rectangular holes in trunks and logs, and may also eat fruits and nuts.
